THE RIDER — ENORMOUS, SERIOUS, WRONG
A Japanese man of monstrous size, close to three metres seated, so broad his shoulders are wider
than the handlebars, so heavy the machine sits low on its springs under him. Everything about his
proportions is a size too large for the world around him.

His face is painted deep matt vermilion, real greasepaint on real weathered skin, thick in the
creases and rubbed thin over the cheekbones, streaked where sweat has run through it. A long
straight prosthetic nose strapped over his own, moulded resin with a visible seam and a strap mark
pressed into the paint. Wild white hair and a long white beard, coarse, matted, blown back. Two
short blunt horns of real yellowed bone lashed to his forehead with cord. Deep-set black eyes,
entirely calm. He is not performing. He believes this completely.

CLOTHING — ASCETIC ROBES ADAPTED FOR RACING
The heavy undyed hemp robes of a mountain ascetic in oatmeal and charcoal, coarse open weave, but
cut short and strapped down for speed: the skirts hacked off at the knee and bound with tape, the
sleeves cut away at the shoulder, a row of small woollen pom-poms down the front half torn off. A
thick knotted cord round his waist doubled as a racing belt. Over it, plates of scorched black iron
strapped on with leather like improvised armour, dented and rivetted. Cracked leather gauntlets to
the elbow. Tall single-tooth wooden geta bolted to steel footpegs — his feet are still in geta, and
the wood is split and burnt at the edges. A small black lacquered cap tied on with cord, sitting
absurdly on top of all of it.

THE MACHINE — A MEDIEVAL CHOPPER BUILT LIKE AN INSTRUMENT OF TORTURE
An enormous long-forked chopper, twice the length of a normal motorcycle, forged rather than
manufactured — hand-beaten black iron, hammer marks visible, welds left raw, bolts mismatched.
Nothing chrome, nothing polished: pitted metal, scorch marks, rust bleeding at the joins.
The frame is built from parts that were made to hurt people: a rack's iron ratchet wheel as the
front sprocket, a pillory's hinged neck plate as the headstock, wrist shackles hanging from the
crossbar on chains, a barbed iron collar around the headlamp housing, an iron maiden's spiked door
panel cut down and bolted on as the fuel tank, its studs still on the inside. The seat is a hard
narrow iron saddle with no padding. Long forged spikes stand out from the wheel hubs. The exhaust
is a bundle of six blackened pipes swept up like organ pipes, heat-blued and sooted.
Enormous spoked wheels, the rims heavy iron, the tyres thick and worn. Chains everywhere — real
chain, heavy, oiled, hanging in loops.
It is heavy, cruel and ludicrous, and it has clearly been ridden hard: road grime up the flanks,
oil weeping from the cases, one crude hand-welded repair.

THE CONTRADICTION — THIS IS THE POINT
Ancient religious clothing bolted to a machine made of torture hardware, ridden by a man the size
of a house who is entirely, gravely serious about a race. Nothing about it is a joke to him.
